answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: Anna Howard Shaw’s The Story of a Pioneer reports that Anthony ended her final public appeal with these three words. Wikiquote and the Speaking While Female speech transcription place the address at the Baltimore suffrage convention on February 15, 1906. Shaw’s recollection is evidence of the utterance, not proof Anthony invented the three-word phrase.

author.name: Susan B. Anthony
author.heading: About Susan B. Anthony
author.bio: Susan B. Anthony was a reformer whose work centered on women’s voting rights. She collaborated with Elizabeth Cady Stanton in organizing, publishing and campaigning, and also worked in the abolitionist movement. Her arguments linked political representation with women’s economic and personal independence.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: The words close an appeal to women to continue the suffrage campaign. Shaw describes Anthony speaking despite weakness and asking others to carry on the cause. The historical setting is political organizing, not a general promise that every personal undertaking must succeed. Shaw memoir, chapter X ↗
